value.body: An archivist preserves, catalogues and provides access to historical records such as manuscripts, files, photographs and maps. Employers include national and state archives, museums, universities, research institutes and some large organisations with record rooms. A typical day involves sorting and describing documents, supervising conservation and digitisation, and helping researchers find material.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A. History, then an M.A. or diploma in archival studies

items.label: Training
items.value: Diploma/certificate courses in archives keeping are offered by the National Archives of India

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Cataloguing standards, digitisation equipment, records databases

items.label: National Archives of India holdings
items.note: Other public statements give higher totals

items.label: Pages digitised by NAI
items.note: Available through the Abhilekh Patal portal

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most entrants add a postgraduate degree or a diploma in archival studies after a B.A. History. Government archive posts are filled through recruitment notices or public service commissions; project-based digitisation work is a common first job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Handling and basic conservation of fragile material
Reading old scripts or regional languages

value.title: At a glance
items: A small field with limited openings, many of them in government.
Next roles: assistant archivist, archivist, records manager or curator.
Digitisation projects have added contract work, often short-term.
